tips.comment: Shader runs today at Haydock Park, making his handicap debut after two commanding novice wins over this trip on the all-weather last autumn. He scored by 7½ and 3¾ lengths, suggesting significant potential. Now rated 99, he enters a deeper field but remains unexposed and open to further improvement.

After a couple of decent efforts over hurdles he returned to the flat at Doncaster at the end of March and finished a close up 4th over an extended 10f. He might well have finished even closer had he not been hampered late on and stepped up on that performance when 3rd at Epsom next time, beaten a length. Went even closer last time at York and is likely to give his running again despite a 3lb rise in his mark.
Lieber Power has had a decent enough form boost, you would argue. With Oisin Murphy onboard and the main colours for King Power, this horse should go close.

Shader could be anything on the back of three runs but is handicapped as such. Fox Journey looks very attractively priced. Contested several deeper races than this. Although he comes here after a long layoff, he has won on seasonal return the last two seasons.
Was returning from an 8-month absence when finishing in midfield off a mark of 104 over 12f. Is kept to that trip here, and with that run behind him, should do a lot better. Each way claims.
Has performed well on the AW lately and capable of another good performance if transforming that form on to turf. Runs off a good mark with Harry Davies on board.
Kildare Legend has solid form, and with a run under his belt 20 days ago, must have a big chance to at least finish in the first 5 places.

The form figures of SHAHA read 2141, with the most recent victory coming in the Listed Daisy Warwick Fillies' Stakes (1m4f, good). She was a 1¼l winner that day, but she appeared to have more left than the winning margin would suggest. That effort represented a considerable improvement over her runs prior to that, and she has been given an official rating of 105 for today, significantly higher than the 90 she had last time out. Along with Estranged, she is one of the least exposed in the field. Therefore, there is every chance that she is much better than her current mark would indicate. There appears to be plenty of pace in the race, which will suit, and this daughter of Cracksman has strong claims of giving the yard a consecutive winner of this race.

Still looked raw and still looked like she could take another step forward when winning at Doncaster in soft ground staying on much the best. Has plenty to prove on different ground and any move in the market would be significant.
Runner-up over the extended mile and a quarter at York in a Group 2 last time out and likely to welcome the step up in trip and ease in class to Group 3.

Trying to get a few in early, and I am still losing the prices. I suppose it's a good sign that this is coming in, and Audience, which I don't fancy at all, is going out. Trainer going well, and 7-2 is still ok. Might have an ew tomorrow.

Drop back to 6f and being held up was no help to him on his sole start of the year at Meydan. This should suit him much better, especially if they decide to go back to more forceful tactics. He was a Group 1 winner last year and this is a Group 3.

Frankel's half-brother Kikkuli looks interesting in this Haydock Group 3. Runner-up in his only start as a juvenile, he won a maiden on seasonal debut last April before finishing second in a Listed race at Sandown and beaten a short head in the Group 3 Jersey Stakes at Royal Ascot. He failed to place in his 3 subsequent starts, but they were at Group 1 and 2 level. He returned from 7 months off when 4th in a Listed race over course and distance. He was impeded at the start there but was beaten just 2 lengths. Oisin Murphy, who rode him in the Jersey Stakes, is back on board, and at these odds, he has to be worth an EW bet.

Ten Bob Tony showed real class when finishing second in a Group 3 at Longchamp last autumn, but hasn’t looked the same in two runs since. He’s been freshened up and returns here with top jockey William Buick booked, which could spark a revival. EW shout.

This looks more open than the market suggests to me, and I thought Volterra could be the most interesting in here. He won when last seen, having quickened up really smartly over this trip at Ascot. He won’t get it his own way in front here, but that said, he could appreciate a strong pace on that evidence as he won in a decent enough time there given the soft ground. That does suggest also he might want ground on the softer side even if he is 2/3 on Good, but with a mark of 103 and two Group 1 entries, the yard must have some optimism that he could improve as a 4yo. So I’m taking on the principles here.

Room Service impressed last autumn, handling tough conditions well to win a listed race at Doncaster after a solid effort at York. He didn’t fire in the Greenham over 7 furlongs last year, but that was a hot race and came early in his development. If he settles into the race, he’s got the quality to land a blow. A strong each-way with win potential.

Really interesting Listed contest over seven furlongs. Quite a few up and coming four year old sorts. Alyanaabi merits respect. Harry Angel mare Tiger Bay (five years old actually) has the lowest weight in the race. She won a Listed race for fillies much earlier this month. Goes a step higher to Group 3 competition here. Lots of strong handicap form. Stays seven furlongs and good ground will suit plus the mare's allowance will come in handy.
Quinault is still progressing in my reading of his races. Down in class here and running on more suitable ground, i.e., softish, he is one with a chance here at decent odds.

Al Shababi runs today at Haydock after a dominant maiden win at Windsor last month. That effort earned him a Racing Post Rating of 95, and he now steps into handicaps off a mark of 82. Lightly raced and progressive, he looks set for a big run.

There are many promising 3yos meeting here in this Class 4 0-85 handicap over 1 mile. City Of God's run in the Class 2 Silver Bowl over course and distance a week ago has to rank as high form. He was headed a long way out when taking quite a wide course in the straight and ultimately did very well to finish within five lengths of the winner. Karl Burke (SR 17%) trained Kodiac colt out of a Galileo mare. Looks to have both speed and stamina and is very much a contender officially down in grade here.

Criminal Shore has improved for switching to handicaps, winning at Ripon and then finishing a good second at Goodwood. That could turn out to be a decent race (6th won on next start). This looks a tough race, but with potential for more improvement, he looks a fair price.

Difficult race to call with a case to be made for a few of these, but a chance is taken on Jasour to return to winning ways after wind surgery. Balmoral Lady is worth a look at the prices E/W after a solid reappearance.
Leovanni is proven to like these quicker conditions and the Burke yard is in fine form. All runners have question marks, but Leovanni less so

Balmoral Lady has a very consistent record and appears to perform on all types of going. Ran well last time out from a poor draw at Chester and has been placed at listed level last season at Doncaster.

Was very consistent last year running some cracking races in good company and got stronger and better as the season went on. Won twice last year including over C&D in a very fast time with the likes of American Affair behind and that one has come out this season to make the form look strong. Has run well on both starts this season including when fourth to American Affair at York last time. Yard starting to click and had a nice double on Wednesday so all in all this one looks to have a lovely chance from a fair draw and should handle the step up in grade. Real soft ground would be a worry if it rained but dam was a 7f winner on heavy ground so should be ok. Lots to like and I think is a decent EW play at the prices.

Leovanni looks like the only 3yo in this race, so gets weight from all and could well be using this as a prep run for the Commonwealth Cup. If so, it could be worth looking at Rage Of Bamby. Lost a shoe on seasonal debut in the Group 2 Duke Of York, which was a tough race anyway and should hopefully be more spot on this time out. I might come back with Leovanni as my win tip.

Durham Castle missed an engagement earlier in the week in a weaker race than this. It could be significant that he runs here. Least experienced of these, and although he comes here on the back of a lengthy layoff of 270 days, this mark looks attractive.

Trying to get some in early, and old Kings Lynn with Oisin back on top looks a decent each way. Back down in trip from last time out and dropping into a class 3 race means even this 8-year-old could still be in the mix.

Kodi Lion had a solid three-year-old season with two wins and has picked up right where he left off, finishing runner-up in competitive handicaps at Doncaster and Ascot. Now with new connections after changing hands for 90,000 guineas, he’s clearly thought of as a horse with more to give. He’s consistent, in form, and still improving. Should be right in the mix again and looks a strong each-way shout with definite win potential if things go smoothly.
Pals Battalion somehow got blocked on the six-lane motorway at Doncaster recently by Danny Nohope before it had a terrific burst of speed, just denied. Big chance for recompense here.

Trilby shaped better than the result last time out at York in a better race than this. He drops in class here. In class 3s, he has a win and 3 placed efforts from 5 starts, and he has 3 wins and a second from 5 runs at the track. The yard is going at 21% in the last 14 days and does well at the track. He is worth an interest with the extra place.

Dakota Gold is knocking on a bit now but has found his form again, finishing 2nd of 10 over 5f on Soft in a Class 2 in October. He followed that up with a win over 6f from 13 runners in a Class 3 in his season's opener and usually improves by his second race. His mark has gone up by 3 lbs for the win but he has won over marks in the 100s during his career. Conor Beasley has been in the saddle for all but six of his 72 races, so he should know his horse well and is used to big fields, including wins.

A 4-year-old, he has finished in the first two 5 times from 12 starts on turf, winning 4 times over 5-6 furlongs. 4th of 13 at Newcastle over 6 furlongs earlier this month, he can run well here in first-time cheekpieces, on good going.

A 17 runner Class 3 handicap over six furlongs at Haydock Park looks fun. Bosh is up to this level and down to a more reasonable handicap mark of 87. Makes third start for Michael Dods here (won handicaps off marks of 88 and 90 when with Richard Hannon). Paul Mulrennan rides. By Group 1 winning sprinter Profitable. Good racing ground should suit. Central draw in stall 9. Must improve on his three recent outings for this yard but always been an in and out type, very useful on his day. Three of his four wins have come at this grade. Chance.

Looks like the lively outsider in the field, and dropping back to 6f could be a good move back on turf. Has beaten DRAGON ICON over 7f and has ability with the yard in form. Rab Havlin will be riding with intent today. E/w play.

Race 6 at Kempton today is the Betfred Fillies' Handicap (Class 3) for 3-year-olds and upwards over 1,442 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 3yo filly Oolong Poobong from the Edward Bethell yard, and will be ridden by Connor Beasley. This daughter of Make Believe is a one-time winner from 5 starts to date. However, in effect, she could easily have been a three-time winner with her last two defeats being by the shortest of margins. In hindsight, she should be the one to beat and should not be ignored.

A couple of good wins last year. Returned from absence to finish 6th of 12 at Musselburgh when possibly needing the run but also was short of room. Met more trouble in running last time out when 4th. Stayed on despite being denied a clear run repeatedly from 3 out. Worth another chance, and if getting a clear run today, may well get involved with Buick on board.

Zouky runs today at Haydock, making her stable debut after a ten-month layoff. She previously secured a win at Newbury and placed in a German Listed race, demonstrating her capability at higher levels. Now rated 87, she returns to a course where she has past success, suggesting she could be competitive if fully fit.

Expensive purchase from the De Bromhead yard in the winter and didn't show much in Dubai last time. But the market support is telling and a fillies race looks a good place to start in the UK. Great chance.

Sueno runs today at York, stepping into Group 3 company after a solid fourth in a Listed race at Goodwood earlier this month. That effort came after a lengthy layoff, and she was noted for making late headway despite a troubled passage. With just four career starts, she remains unexposed and is open to further improvement.

Scenic ran on strongly last time to be a respectable 2nd to a Gosden one. Tardy at the start and took some time to warm to it, it can be put down to needing the run after a break. Only has to be slightly more alert here to get involved at the finish and possibly go one better.
Crystal Flyer arrives on the back of some good form with three wins and two seconds in the last six outings and could get involved here at a generous looking price.

Urban Glimpse runs today at York, stepping up to Class 3 company after a promising handicap debut at Sandown last month. He finished second in that race, beaten just over two lengths, and has been raised 2lb to a mark of 85. With only four career starts, including a win at Kempton, he remains unexposed and open to further improvement.

Cape Breton got home well at Ascot when not looking the most straightforward ride. He can learn from that to make a mark here, and he could do so from a fairly uncontested forward position. The worry in that regard is Ryan Moore dictating on Munsif, who won as he liked last time but looks too short for me. With a bit more experience under his belt, I think Cape Breton can take a step forward here, with his conqueror last time being more than race fit, having had a couple of starts so far this season.

Looks Fantastic shaped nicely when fourth at Leicester, staying on late after finding the 7 furlongs a bit sharp. This step back up in trip looks a positive move, and now tackling handicaps for the first time, he should be more competitive. Still learning but there’s definitely ability there. With the longer trip to help him settle and finish stronger, he looks a lively each-way chance.

Had won on his first start for this yard at Kempton last November and returned with a fair effort at Newmarket at the beginning of the month over a mile. Appeared to just run to a similar level at Newbury last time but found himself short of room on more than one occasion. Hopefully that won’t be the case today and can reward each way support.

I think this one is a standout bet here in this race that doesn't quite look the deepest to me and certainly isn't any stronger than the races this fella has been competing in this season. Has unfortunately bumped into American Affair the last twice including over C&D and has clocked very fast times in defeat. That horse has since run well enough in the Group 2 Temple Stakes and will win a big pot this year I'm sure so JM Jungle's form stands out. Is a C&D winner to boot and though up another 3lb from last effort could be classy enough to handle the rise. Must go close and was nearly the Nap of the day for me but that honour goes to Shagraan who was just behind this one at York last time and could make the form look much stronger about twenty minutes earlier over at Haydock.

Gelded back in October and has raced twice since, with a much improved showing here two weeks ago when 2nd of twenty-two runners. The drop back to five furlongs would have helped with a win last year at this distance. Still unexposed, and a two-pound rise might not have any effect at all for a progressive horse.

Venture Capital deserves his chance at this race today, given the speed and authority shown on last start against quality animals. A few in this race have never really suited being against these kinds of peers, and I think the booking of Ryan Moore is also a positive here.

Smart performer who landed a 7th career victory when winning at Newcastle last summer. Remained in decent form thereafter and has made steady improvement so far this spring, with the best performance so far coming when 5th over 6 furlongs here last time. Down another lb, so should run well this afternoon.

Zayer gets pitched in against older horses, having never really landed a blow on handicap debut against his age group. He and Loom get 8 lbs from their elders, and both make appeal in that regard. But I am going to follow Zayer again, who I just think should be well handicapped enough to get involved. He didn’t get the best of runs, having missed the break slightly last time, and then got stuck behind a bit of a wall. Hopefully, he’ll improve for it, and he’s lost a lb too, which is a bonus given he wasn’t given a hard time of it late on but still stuck to the task. He was giving a stone to a subsequent winner there, and he’s drawn around the principles, which can hopefully drag him into the shake-up. He’s bred to potentially appreciate a bit further, so he should appreciate a strong pace if he can go with it (he’s 4th on speed ratings in here).

I got interrupted when trying to put up this tip earlier and once again have lost the price. It was still 22-1 when I started, but is still 18-1 with 365, so not all is lost. Hasn't had a run this season, but has changed trainers and this one is in form with his small brigade. I'm hoping Mr. Oldroyd can turn this one around and turn him back into the horse he once was.
Over on the Gravesmire, another Domera runner, which also got blocked here somehow on the rail, finishing with its head in its chest, is Riot. Should go better on that evidence.

Delicacy who I backed last time is no price here but is still interesting again. The market suggests that’s the race to follow given the top four in the market are out of that race. I’m happy to side elsewhere in a wide open handicap that 4yo’s generally dominate having won 9/10 renewals. Interestingly 6/10 have been won by claiming jockeys so that’s possibly an angle in, and a pair of them intrigue in the shape of Ziggys Condor and Daring Legend. The former has an interesting record here, but I’d have a slight worry that he won’t quite get home. He could set up the pace for Daring Legend who should have no such staying worries, and with him towards the bottom of these weights adjusted for claim he ended up taking my interest. He was ahead of a subsequent winner last time, and the winner has placed since too. His peak turf RPR came with this jockey aboard which is a plus, and conditions look perfect for a solid run.

Race 7 at York today is the William Hill Best Odds Guaranteed Handicap (Class 4) for 4-year-olds and upwards over 1,408 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 4-year-old gelding Ziggys Condor from the Richard Fahey yard, and will be ridden by Warren Fentiman. This son of Havana Grey is a consistent enough performer and has top runs at this track behind his name, including a shortest of margins 2nd here almost exactly one year ago in the Conundrum Handicap. He should be a bold runner again and not to be ignored.

Winning is no longer straight forward these days for this 6-year-old, but he did manage to get back on track from a more lenient mark with blinkers back on, finishing 2nd in a handicap at Redcar 12 days ago. He is clearly on a competitive mark, but the distance winner might have to take back seat again, which should still result in a decent profit with an each-way bet at 20/1.

BEATTIE IS BACK has run 22 races, and all 3 of his career victories have come on all-weather (Newcastle x2 and Wolverhampton). He was tried in cheekpieces and blinkers recently, but they came off last time out, and he returned to form when fourth of 12 in a 7f handicap at Ayr last month. The headgear remains off for this. Apprentice Ethan Tindall takes over for the first time, and his 7lb claim will come in handy. Three of the jockey's winners this year have come for Richard Fahey.

Ex Irish, who has only had 4 starts for Jedd O'Keeffe, has been rather good without winning. His latest effort at Haydock 21 days ago, when 3rd of 12 beaten a length, was useful and over 7f, which suggests he should be finishing to some effect over this straight galloping 6f. Hector Crouch takes over today, and with 6 places on offer, he looks an each-way shout.

Made a successful seasonal return at Thirsk in April. Secured a commendable 4th position among 10 in a handicap at Ripon 22 days prior. With blinkers back on and Alan Brown's yard in excellent form, an each-way bet at 18/1 seems favourable for this distance winner.

Didn't manage to win last season but generally ran quite consistently and took a step forward from reappearance when 4th at Musselburgh last time. Down another lb for that and will surely be striking soon.

I mean there's plenty you can make claims for in a fiercely competitive handicap here. I think TRUE PROMISE has a combo of being handily drawn, a likely front runner, and looks to have a run within this mark. Throw in a claimer taking further weight off, who has got him close before, and maybe this price holds some value.

Tempted by Beyond Borders, who has been campaigned interestingly so far this season. Races have been at idiosyncratic Ripon, where this horse has failed to settle both times. This is a much reduced mark, and I think could really capitalize here.
Coul Angel ran a cracker of a race last time out, and that looks to have a bit of strength in depth in it. With 6 places here, I'm sure he can hit the frame.

Another handicap with plenty of places on offer. So, looking at some value, I've sided with the very lightly raced Singoura. Twice a runner-up and a win from her 3 starts to date, with the latest (only start this year) when 2nd of 5 at Donny late April. Only second handicap start and now with a very good 5lb claimer, can hopefully make her competitive.

Been running consistently well, and although only 5th last time, it was a bunch finish, and Frankie's Dream finished off the race strongly. That race was in a better grade and should be in the mix today for trainer Jennie Candish and is back racing after just 17 days' rest.

50-1 Richard Fahey trained selection over seven furlongs at York... nice! Tuscan Point is yet to win but hasn't seen too much racing action. Five of his seven runs have come at York. Seems to meet trouble in running quite a bit. Back up to preferred seven furlongs now from five furlongs run here last time. Billy Garritty rides this Blue Point gelding. Likely value at this price in an open race.
Good 2nd first time up, then even better in an Ascot novice next time when third, as it seemed a very good race and should be up to winning this.

He’s already got a win on the board and TRICKY TEL should use that experience to good use here. Come On Over carries a poor FlatStats rating alongside Amo Racing’s poor 2/22 record (A/E 0.31) with fancied runners on tight courses, meanwhile Going Commando bares an even worse FS rating and A Keatley’s 4% SR (A/E 0.4) with moderately fancied runners tempers enthusiasm further. Starman’s first crop have flattered to deceive so far (10% SR, A/E 0.45) so I’m not expecting a step forward from Goldenstateofmind and I can’t make a case for the rest. TT couldn’t have won any more comfortably on debut here at Chester over 5.5f at the beginning of the month; he’s got a 6lb penalty to carry for that but the 3rd and 4th have since gone on to win, suggesting that the form might prove useful. The son of Ubettabelieveit carries a top + blue FS rating plus a couple of positive stats boost claims further; most notable being H Palmer’s 67% SR (A/E 1.49) with 2yo favourites at Chester and the breeder’s general 23% SR (A/E 1.62). 13/8 taken.

Race 3 at Chester today is the British Stallion Studs EBF Novice Stakes (Class 2) for 2-year-olds over 1,223m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 2yo colt Goldenstateofmind from the David Loughnane yard, and will be ridden by Jack Mitchell. This son of Starman had an eye-opening debut when a good 2nd over 1000m and gave the impression that he will be much sharper over a little further, which he gets today. In the Team Valor silks, the colt looks like the one to beat in this field.

Yellow Card heads to Chester today aiming for a hat-trick after back-to-back wins at Wolverhampton and Salisbury. He’s up 7lb but still looks ahead of the handicapper and has drawn stall 1, which is a big plus around this track. If he handles the tighter turns, he should take all the beating.

Race 4 at Chester today is the King Kabs Handicap (Class 4) for 4-year-olds and upwards over 3,197 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 5-year-old mare Dreams Adozen from the Charlie Johnston yard, and she will be ridden by Joe Fanning. She usually runs well here with two wins and a string of close finishes in her visits. She is distance-suited and caught the eye in her latest when a close 4th here. Big chance on all known form.

I am picking Spirit of Acklam in this race as it managed to win its last race, which was a class 4 handicap, by 2 lengths off a rating of 79. This is also a class 4 handicap, but it is running off a rating of 83. Given the winning distance, I am hoping it can still perform well in this race. It has got a decent record in flat races on turf so far in its career, running 8 times, and it has managed to win 3 of them as well as placing in 1.
Made headway inside the final furlong over the extended mile and a quarter here earlier this month and should welcome the extra 2 furlongs.

In a wide-open Class 4, 10-runner handicap, a chance is taken on the Ed Walker-trained Miss Alpilles. She looked in need of her comeback run at Newcastle 20 days ago, finishing a well-beaten 8/11. However, that was in Class 3 handicap company, and she has been dropped 2 lbs, leaving her with room off 79. She would have stepped forward plenty for that run, will love the ground, gets the trip, and at 16/1 could be a spot of each-way value.

Two wins and three places from eight career outings. Excuses last time out when the ground conditions were probably too soft. Looks to have strong claims here, making a debut for a new yard with a previous course win a positive here at Chester.
Has won 3 and finished 2nd in 2 of 8 starts to date, with 1 of the wins being here in June last year. Likely to go well again and holds at least an each-way chance.
Eddie Greaterex has four good chances here today, but I like this CD winner Fair Point, hoping it's progressed for Ralf Beckett

Contrary to what ITV would have you believe, there is only a small draw bias over the 7f track here according to the stats. It makes it quite possible to get a nice price on ones drawn wide, and Myal went from 6/1 overnight to 9/1 when the draw was done. What there is a bias for here at Chester is pace, and it's the hardest course in the country to come from off the pace. There aren't many real front runners here though, so he should be able to get over fine from the wider draw, and I'd be very surprised to see him far from the front. A serious run in the Spring Mile when the only one of the leaders to finish better than 17th, the others in 18th, 20th, and 21st, and duly followed that up with a nice win at Haydock where it's notoriously hard to lead. 8th latest in the Victoria Mile, a much deeper race than this appears. Never So Brave and Fair Point are the main concerns; however, with neither having had a run, they are easy to oppose, and this looks tailor-made for him.

Lowest he has been in the handicap since winning the Buckingham Palace Stakes at Royal Ascot in 2023. Has a tidy draw on the inside and produced a fair effort in the Victoria Cup last time out from a couple of pounds higher.

Yaniker won here from stall twelve. Today, he has to do the same play from stall ten, which could be achieved with Aiden Brooks taking three pounds off and making a quick move to get a good position to be able to serve a big run up. Trainer Garriet Bethell can have her charge having this as his second run of the season after a run here twenty-two days ago, with a seventh place behind Two Tempting. He is only three pounds higher than his best winning mark of 89, but taking the jockey claim into consideration, he is really racing off this. Plus, he is bottom-weighted here, getting a stone from Witch Hunter.

Plenty miles on the clock for the 7yo but he does have 9 turf wins to his name. Two return runs last month should have sharpened him up. Every chance at this level and a bit of give in the ground will suit him. His decent draw at this Chester track is a plus. Good apprentice in the saddle and his claim puts him on an attractive mark.

The Tom Dascombe-trained Seraphim Angel has 2 wins from 7 turf runs. The 3-year-old Sergei Prokofiev filly didn't get a clear run here last time out, finishing 4th. She has a great draw in trap 1, and 2-time winning jockey Pierre-Louis Jamin is back in the saddle with a big run anticipated.

Has 3 wins over this trip , 2 on the turf & other on all weather one win came 2 runs ago at Ripon class 5 over 6f . She finished 6th in class 4 at Windsor 26 days ago doing top much early on & running out of steam . She wears 1st time cheekpieces today & to hopefully get back on track .

Magellan Cloud runs today at Chester, stepping up in trip after consecutive third-place finishes at Musselburgh and Haydock. He was beaten just over four lengths last time and now races off a mark of 79. His sole win came over seven furlongs on soft ground, but his pedigree suggests he should handle this longer distance. With a solid draw and consistent form, he enters this race with credible claims.
War Hawk is drawn well, has been consistent, and the only drawback is this horse's run style normally. However, it looks progressive and could feature here.

Race 7 at Chester today is the Going Is Good Handicap (Div 1) (Class 4) for 3-year-olds over 2,076 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 3-year-old filly Wilhelmina from the Kevin Philippart de Foy yard, and will be ridden by top jockey Daniel Muscutt.

Master Zack runs today at Southwell, returning to the scene of his April win over this course and distance. He was hampered early when third on turf at Bath last time, but his prior Tapeta form suggests a return to this surface will suit. Now rated 52, he remains well-handicapped and is the only runner in the field with a C&D victory.

The inform Richard Hannon-trained She Went Whoosh is his only runner on the card. The 3-year-old Profitable filly has 1 win and 1 place from 4 runs on the AW. The game changer is young Tyrese Cameron, who takes off 7 lbs, leaving him with second bottom weight on 7-13.
A course and distance winner off this mark of 58 back in April 2024 and likely to appreciate the drop in trip after racing over 2 miles on the turf at Nottingham earlier this month.

Showed a lot of heart on debut at Wolverhampton over 1m 4f, completely missing the break and running very green, had to be pushed by the jockey for basically a full circuit and held on strongly into the finish. A fair amount of improvement would not be entirely unexpected.

Sottsass filly. A half-sister to the 7f/1m Victor Rogue Force and the 2-year-old 7.4 winner Emily's Eclipse. Her dam is an unraced half-sister to the impressive 1m winner Princess Loulou. She will don a hood for her debut, which is significant given the trainer's success with horses wearing first-time headgear, along with an excellent track record when entering a single horse at a flat meeting. The 28/1 each-way odds seem spot on.

It has been 12 races since his last win in 2024, but the 4-year-old faced a significant challenge with first-time cheekpieces, finishing 19th at York in a handicap in his last outing. On the other hand, trainer Scott Dixon has a commendable record at Southwell, with 43 wins and 160 placements over the last 5 seasons here. Given the odds of 25/1, an each-way bet looks to be a solid chance for profit.
Alligator Alley was a big eye-catcher on turf last time at Thirsk when it also got blocked before coming around them, finishing hands and heels. Ruth Carr will get a win from this, maybe today.

Iskar D'Airy has won 2 of his 5 starts over fences. He won at Huntingdon in March off 87 and, having finished second at Hereford off 94, won at Warwick last month off 96. He is up another 8 lbs, but all those runs were on good ground, so the recent rain will help, and he looks to have a great chance again.

The model I run suggests Never Seen Again can win this one. Never Seen Again lines up here with a fairly middle order RPR but goes out carrying a reasonable weight compared to the rest of the runners. The Old Bridge is already incredibly short-priced, and so this looks like the best value bet. The model has suggested a 'very low' staking indicator here, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

The model I run suggests Bethpage can win this one. Bethpage lines up with only the second highest RPR of the 6 runners here, but all RPR scores are tightly bunched. The official ranking is similar, but Bethpage comes here in the best form of the 6 runners. 2012 form figures and looks to get the nose in front here first over this longer 3m trip. The model has issued a 'very low' staking indicator largely driven by the value of this at 2/1. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4 in the system.

I was on Up For Parol in his last few starts since he last won in a Class 3 over 3m back in January at Ffos Las. He has run consistently the last three times, but he hasn't had things fall his way. The track, trip, and ground should all suit. He was only beaten 2 lengths on Monday at Cartmel in a £30k race, when staying on all the way to the line but was too far out of his ground early on. If this doesn't come too soon, then he should have every chance of running another big race.
Ran well last time out on his return from a break. Won well here last September and looks to have a good chance here.

Game when landing a handicap by 1 1/4 off 110 over 3m 2f at Fontwell last time. Should come on for that; trainer in form; prefers a sharp track; good strike rate; needs stiff test but go close if getting it.

The model I run suggests Romanor can win this one. Romanor sets out with the second highest RPR of this much smaller 6 runner field but has an official ranking leaving him very well treated. Goes out carrying the lowest initial amount of weight compared to all the other runners. Romanor comes here in good form, placing 16 days ago and looks to build on that here. Romanor is a previous course and distance winner, so knows how to get it done around this track. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which is largely driven by the small gap back to second in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Won this last year off 5 lb higher, and the latest run really was a tender ride. I honestly think it could go off favorite, and the pricing is crazy with cheekpieces back on.

Ajp Kingdom may not have been at his best last time at Market Rasen, but that run came just eight days after a solid effort and might have come too soon. He’s already shown he stays well with a win over 3m2f, and back on a more suitable schedule, he could bounce back. He has the stamina and enough ability and is not one to dismiss lightly. EW claims if he returns to his better form here.

Stage Show put in a solid effort when finishing second at Taunton, showing a bit more grit than in previous runs. That was a step in the right direction and proves he’s capable when things go his way. If he runs to a similar level again, he should be right in the mix. Needs to back it up and looks a strong each-way player.

Zoran won his last hurdles start at Southwell over 2m4f in November and is interesting stepping up to 2m6f for the first time. He won on the flat in January, and although disappointing last month, that was his first start for 64 days, so he probably needed the run. He looks a good each-way bet here with 4 places on offer.

A chance is taken on the rank outsider Leading Lion in the last at Stratford. Comfortable winner of a handicap hurdle at Bellewstown (2m4f, Good) for Gordon Elliott last August off OR100. Struggled at long odds in two races since joining the small yard of Tracey Leeson (has had one winner from just three runners this season). 7lbs claiming amateur jockey up again. Some chance of improvement for this second race back from wind surgery. Longer trip and officially drops down in class.

I'm opting for Amberelli in this Class 5 Mares Handicap Hurdle. She travelled very well for a long way at Ludlow last time out so this drop back in trip should suit her (5f less). Sean Bowen booked again. She could go well.

The model I run suggests Opticality can win this one. Opticality lines up here with a relatively high RPR in what looks like a reasonably open race. The official ranking is second highest, but the weight being carried is the second lowest here in this 9-runner field around this 2m round trip. The model has issued a 'very low' staking indicator largely as a result of the small gap back to second in the race simulation. this translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Cavalry Call lines up at Lingfield Park today in excellent form, having finished first or second in his last four starts. He followed a Chelmsford win with a close runner-up effort at Windsor just 12 days ago, showing strong consistency. A current mark of 79 reflects his progress, and he’s proven under similar conditions. With stamina assured and the ground to suit, he looks primed to go close again.

Meet Me In Meraki has found himself an excellent opportunity to bounce back and strongly appeals as the type to do so was last seen at Southwell 31 days ago where finishing 8th/10 in an amateur jockeys handicap that wasn't the best of run to suit his nature of going however this race is a whole different scenario and he has had 31 days to get over thay last run dropping in trip racing at the 1 mile 2 furlong trip here that being a good move by his connections as P D Evans's inmate can be shown to best effect at this trip especially switching to the suitable turf track here at Lingfield which can play well into the strengths of Meet Me In Meraki here and is likely to get his favoured pace level in a race of this nature too and with his mark continuing to ease now operating on a mark of 61 he looks poised for a big run here jockey J F Egan takes the ride and can ensure Meet Me In Meraki gets the best possible outcome here

City Cyclone runs today at Lingfield Park following a win at Wolverhampton and a narrow second at this track earlier this month. He’s now won three of his last eight and continues to improve, rising to a career-high mark of 73. Although all victories have come on the all-weather, his latest effort on turf was encouraging.

Thapa Vc put in a very impressive performance when last seen at Bath 26 days ago where he won going away and really looked to have enjoyed that outing very much in the process and all he needed was just one tap of the whip and he was off and gone inside the closing stages on that race has only been risen 2lb by the accesor and is now operating on a mark of 69 however that small rise is of no concern and in my point of view Thapa Vc is likely to still be a good step ahead of the accesor here and having found himself another suitable looking assignment here that shouldn't take much winning as it does look to be a thin class 5 handicap where Thapa Vc can gain another well deserved success jockey Callum Shepherd takes the ride on M G Rimell's inmate and can give him a promising ride here at Lingfield must be considered

Mart must be considered a very serious contender here and for very good reason was last seen over this course and distance 11 days ago where finishing a promising 2nd/4 and was only just denied the win as he was only beaten 0.1 lengths by the eventual winner and has found an excellent opportunity to go a place better this time out as the handicapper has left his mark un touched and must be taken very seriously racing of the same mark here that being a mark of 70 and worth noting he is operating a total of 5lb below his last winning mark and looks poised to strike in a suitable assignment going on ideal ground conditions here jockey Morgan Cole takes off a handy 3lb which only enhances his good looking claims here merits serious consideration

Back in Easy Company, after first excellent win on debut run of hurdles with top winning jockey back in the saddle, should spark winning streak here. Since the first win by 5 lengths, a few rivals behind that day have won.
Royal Eagle is better value than the favorite, and Gordon Elliott trained the winner of this race last year. The jockey claims 7lb.
Below par 9l third in a maiden hurdle over 2m4f at Fairyhouse most recent run. Dual French flat winner; cheekpieces first time. The one to beat if handling the quicker ground.

Kainsbourg has run creditably in some good races and his full brother Love Me Tender bolted up first time out in a bumper last night, but ultimately he has been a shade disappointing. The Store Boy really stands out as a good alternative, as he has a fantastic pedigree, is trained by a great trainer and is owned by one of his top owners. On paper he could be useful.

Met Office has shown a fair level on the flat, staying on well over trips just short of 1m4f, and brings a decent engine to this new hurdle challenge. Now with a new yard and fitted with a hood, if he takes to jumping, there’s enough ability in him. But he is a bit of a wildcard here and not without each-way hope if adapting to hurdles.
Winner of a point to point over 3m before making the frame in his two runs over hurdles. Step up in trip should be no problem.

Reiki Revolution shaped with some promise on his hurdling debut at Killarney, staying on for fourth in a small field after a break and stable switch. That run should bring him on nicely, and the way he went about things suggests there’s improvement to come and could sneak into the frame here with an each-way place.

Bit Too Much had too much to do, finishing second, beaten by 3 1/2 lengths in a beginners' chase over 2m4f at Kilbeggan last time, where it was given a very gentle ride. It was a useful handicap hurdler prior. Needs much further ideally but can get involved.
After the win last time over hurdles, I think that connections have found an easy enough race to start off here over the larger obstacles and can capitalize here.

Well bred and in the best of hands but went decidely off the boil over hurdles last winter. Interesting to see her tried over fences now after a break. She will doubtless know the job and is taken to return to winning ways.

The model I run suggests Samba Train should win this one. This result has been driven by Samba Train having a relatively high RPR compared to the other runners and is not punished for it in the weights. Goes out carrying the same initial amount of weight as the other runners. There are other claiming jockeys, which Samba Train does not have, which might be something to be concerned about. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Not done a whole lot wrong in three previous bumpers registering two second place finishes against similar opposition to today's so an obvious chance on form and the booking of a top amateur pilot catches the eye. Solid ew bet.

There are some nicely bred horses in this race and at a good price Courtmac Gesture looks interesting. He ran a nice race on his debut to finish a staying on 3rd at Clonmel and he is a Walk In The Park half brother to Barra Rua, who ran a race full of promise to finish second first time out a couple of days ago.
Liadawn has got a lovely pedigree being by Jukebox Jury and out of a Shantou mare with loads of winners in the bloodline. This looks like another winner for the maestro Willie Mullins.

The model I run suggests Early Bird can win this one. Early Bird has the highest RPR of the runners here and lines up carrying the same weight as the majority of runners. Last ran 89 days ago, so race fitness might be a concern, but Mr. Ryan picks up the reins and relieves a further 7 lbs, which is helpful. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator for this, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Sonnyboyliston is trained by C Byrnes, who does well with ex-flat horses. The 8-year-old has won 6 from 11 on the flat and brings plenty of class.

The model I run suggests a win for Wholelotofbusiness. This result has been driven by Wholelotofbusiness having the highest RPR of this 13-runner field. Goes out carrying the same weight as nearly every other runner over this 2m trip with Miss Noonan on board, relieving a further 5 lbs, which is helpful. Placed well 20 days ago with a good second and can build on that here. The model has issued a 'low' stake indicator and sees 5s as good value, but only a small gap back to second in the race simulation. A 'low' stake bet translates to a 0.75pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Has a turn of pace (won four times on the flat) and effort over hurdles last time out was promising. Any improvement on that could well be good enough here but fitness has to be taken on trust.

Willuhaveamineral makes debut in this maiden hurdle for trainer Michael Winters, whose few runners this season have run well and often gone close. This five-year-old Milan mare has some decent relations in the family on the dam's side (Getaway is the grand-dam). A possible if ready to go first time. Daniel King rides.

Aboy Joey is a 6-year-old gelding trained by the in-form Eoin Christopher McCarthy. He is 0-14 wins, opened on a mark of 92, and rose 8lb having finished runner-up on two consecutive starts in handicap hurdles. He finished 2/15 on handicap hurdle debut, beaten 1/2l behind Macinamillion with an RPR of 102, and has since posted a career-high RPR of 121. The 3/15 The Banger Doyle, with an RPR of 110, has since posted a career-high RPR of 138. The 4/15 Whateys Quest posted an RPR of 105, has won twice since, and is rated 111. The 5/15 Duffys Hodey, with an RPR of 84, has won three times since and has posted a career-high RPR of 115. Aboy Joey should be more than capable of winning a handicap hurdle off a mark of 94 under Sean Flanagan, which looks like a significant jockey booking.

Has had his problems (missed the whole of 2024) but prior had looked very useful winning a hurdle and two chase races. Not as good since returning earlier this year but looked a bit more like his old self last time out at Bellewstown and if he is able to build on that he shouldnt be far away.
Lariat is winless in 22 races but is handicapped to go well today. I'm going each way, but a win is not out of the question.

The model I run suggests the each way bet on Mr. Persistence is the value play. Mr. Persistence lines up with the highest RPR of this larger 18-runner field and an official ranking, leaving him well treated on this weight. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator as a result of the small gap back to second in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

The model I run suggests a win for Howdoyalikeherhome. This result has been driven by Howdoyalikeherhome having the highest RPR of this larger 17 runner field and an official ranking that's relatively middle order. This subsequently means less weight being carried over this 2m 4f trip. Good form coming into this with form figures of 41-3 and can build on that here. The model has issued a 'low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.75pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Improving sort. Trip and ground fine today and races off bottom weight so given some more improvement again must hold a place chances at the very least.

Brilliant Light showed ability when winning at Worcester and has the engine to be competitive again. He was far too keen at Down Royal over a longer trip, which took a toll on him late on. Dropping back in distance looks the right call and could help him settle better. If he keeps a lid on things early, he’s capable of getting involved and has a fair each-way chance in this field

Maiden performed admirably after a 7-month break, finishing fifth out of 9 in a handicap hurdle at Killarney just 20 days ago. With Noonan's 5lb claim, the 7-year-old has solid place prospects as he steps back up in distance. An each-way bet at 25/1 appears to be a good value option.

Some improvement this spring over various trips but fair to say has been a bit disappointing over all. However is bred to be much better than anything she's shown us so far and could fare better now handicapping.

Better Than Heaven is interesting at a big price here in a pretty average-looking handicap hurdle. Trainer JP Flavin and 5 lbs claiming jockey Liam McKenna have both had recent winners. The ten-year-old jumped well and was a winner and second over hurdles way back in 2021. Absent since and made first reappearance since then recently. Entitled to come on for that run over two miles and now upped to 2m7f, suggesting he needed that run. Handicap mark six pounds below last winning mark. A hopeful play.

The model I run suggests a value play here might be Game And Glory. Game And Glory lines up here with the highest RPR of this 10-runner field and has the lowest official ranking. This subsequently means he carries far less weight than most runners here. Form leaves a lot to be desired, having been pulled twice in the last 3 races, but has got previous history of being a course winner and a distance winner, so knows how to get it done at this 2m 6f round trip. Price is obviously larger due to the poor recent form, but 25/1 is a big price for someone with history at the course. Last ran 22 days ago and finished that race, so turned around here in quick time. Model indicates a 'very low' staking indicator largely driven by the small gap back to second in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

The model I run suggests an upset by Greenway Machine. This result has been driven by Greenway Machine having the second highest RPR of the larger 14-runner field, but has the lowest official ranking. This leaves him carrying by far the lowest weight around this 2m 6f trip. He is first reserve, but you'd think the chances of one horse pulling out in a 14-horse race is reasonable. Cullinan on board relieves a further 7 lbs, which could be huge over this distance. Last run was 22 days ago, so race fit and comes here as a previous course and distance winner. Model issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt stake on a scale of 0-4.

The model I run suggests Applejack Poet can win this one. Applejack Poet lines up here with a relatively high RPR compared to the other runners in the field but has a comparably low official ranking. This leaves him well treated in the weights relative to potential. One of only two horses in this lineup who have shown any kind of form of late, and came a decent third 18 days ago. Prior distance winner and looks to get it done again. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4. This has been driven by the small gap back to second in the race simulation.

The model I run suggests the value bet here is Hillstar Blues. Hillstar Blues lines up here with the highest RPR of the lineup and is the youngest one here. Goes out carrying the lowest weight over this 2m5f trip, and Danny Power on board relieves a further 7 lbs, which could be telling over the distance. This takes the total weight differential to over 1 stone to the top of the market. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which is a 0.5pt stake on a scale of 0-4.
